reading.title: A School for Everyone
reading.text: In my country, primary education is free for all children. Most families choose a state school because private education is expensive. After secondary education, about half of the students go on to higher education. My older sister is taking a university course in engineering. She says a good education is the best gift parents can give. My grandmother never had the chance to get an education, so she is now studying in an adult education class. She is proud of herself, and so is our whole family.

listening.title: Choosing a School
listening.script: Aziz: Did you decide where your little brother will study? Dilya: Yes. We chose a state school near our house. Primary education there is free, and the teachers are very kind. Aziz: What about the future? Dilya: Well, I hope he gets a good education and goes to university. Higher education is expensive, so my parents are saving money already. Aziz: That is clever. A university education really helps young people find good jobs.

reading.title: My English Course
reading.text: Last month I enrolled on an English course at the language centre. It is an intensive course, so we study every day for three hours. The course fees were not cheap, but my parents agreed that it was a good idea. Two students dropped out after the first week because it was too hard. I want to complete the course and take an exam in the spring. In the course of one month I have learnt many new words, and I can already speak with more confidence.

reading.title: A Lesson to Remember
reading.text: Yesterday we had a science lesson that I will never forget. Our teacher gave a lesson on volcanoes, and she showed us a small model that actually erupted. Everybody paid attention, even the students who usually find lessons boring. I missed the last lesson because I was ill, so my friend explained it to me. In the afternoon I have a swimming lesson, which I enjoy even more. My mother says that every lesson, good or bad, teaches us something.

reading.title: Homework Evenings
reading.text: On school days I come home at four o'clock and have a snack. Then I do my homework at the kitchen table. Our teacher sets a lot of homework, especially in maths, but I try to finish it before dinner. After that I practise the violin for thirty minutes. My teacher says regular practice is more important than long practice once a week. Last Tuesday I forgot to hand in my English homework, so I had to bring it the next day. Now I check my bag every morning.

reading.title: Exam Week
reading.text: Exam week is always a stressful time for students. I have to sit three exams: maths, English and history. For the last two weeks I have been revising every evening, and my mother helps me with my notes. Last year I failed a history exam because I did not read the questions carefully, so this time I will be more careful. The teachers mark the papers quickly, and we get our results on Friday. The pass mark is fifty per cent, but I hope to get a much higher mark. After the exams, our family will go on a picnic.
